questions.prompt: What is the main difference between v-if and v-show?

options.text: v-if toggles CSS display; v-show adds/removes the element
v-if adds/removes the element (and is lazy); v-show only toggles the CSS display property
v-show only works on the server

questions.explanation: v-if truly creates or destroys the element and is lazy; v-show keeps the element in the DOM and just toggles display, making it cheaper to flip frequently.

questions.prompt: Why should each v-for item have a stable, unique :key?

options.text: It's required syntax or the loop won't run
So Vue can match items across updates and reuse/reorder DOM nodes correctly

questions.explanation: The key is a stable identity for each item, letting Vue track items across changes and reuse DOM nodes instead of rebuilding them — preventing subtle state bugs.

questions.prompt: In Vue 3, what happens if you put v-if and v-for on the same element?

options.text: v-for runs first, so v-if can filter each item
v-if has higher priority and runs first, so it can't access the loop variable

questions.explanation: In Vue 3, v-if takes priority over v-for on the same element, so the loop variable isn't available to the condition. Filter with a computed property instead.

questions.prompt: To filter a list before rendering it, do the filtering in a ______ property and loop over the result. (one word)
questions.explanation: Filtering and sorting belong in a computed property; then v-for iterates over the derived list — avoiding the v-if/v-for pitfall.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: v-else must immediately follow a v-if (or v-else-if) element
Using the array index as key is risky for lists that reorder
v-show removes the element from the DOM when false
You can put v-if or v-for on a <template> to group elements without an extra wrapper

questions.explanation: v-else must be adjacent; index-as-key breaks on reorder; and <template> groups elements without a real DOM node. v-show does NOT remove the element — it sets display: none.

questions.prompt: Order these from cheapest to most expensive to TOGGLE repeatedly (visibility on/off many times).
questions.explanation: v-show only flips a CSS property, so it's cheap to toggle repeatedly. v-if creates and destroys the element (and its components/listeners) each time, which costs more per toggle.
